_owner_decision: 2026-07-29, owner-ratified. The brace-expansion trap fired and MEASUREMENT redirected the fix. Chosen: SPLIT. This slice now covers next + postcss ONLY; brace-expansion is deliberately OUT and is closed as a consequence of the separate `eslint-10-migration` slice. WHY brace-expansion cannot be fixed here: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg affects <= 5.0.7 with 5.0.8 as the ONLY patched release, so the v1 branch has no in-range fix. Forcing `brace-expansion@1` to ^5 does not merely cross a major -- it BREAKS AT RUNTIME: v1 is `module.exports = expandTop` (a function) while v5 CJS is `exports.expand` (an object), and the sole consumer minimatch@3.1.5 calls `require('brace-expansion')(...)` as a function. `pnpm install` resolves cleanly and lint dies at call time. WHY the eslint route is the real fix and why it is NOT this slice: eslint@9.39.4 itself depends on minimatch 3.1.5 (with @eslint/config-array@0.21.2 and @eslint/eslintrc@3.3.5), and ^9.18.0 already resolves to the newest 9.x, so nothing inside the ^9 range removes the v1 branch. ESLint v10.0.0 lists `501abd0 feat!: update dependency minimatch to v10 (#20246)` as a breaking change, so v10 drops the branch entirely. That is a major toolchain upgrade with its own compatibility surface (typescript-eslint, @next/eslint-plugin-next, Node floor ^20.19 || ^22.13 || >=24) and it is driven by ESLint v9 END-OF-LIFE on 2026-08-06, not by this advisory. Folding it in here would make this manifest's own `_scope_out` clause 'NO unrelated dependency upgrades riding along' meaningless. ACCEPTED COST: OSV stays red on brace-expansion for the few days between the two slices. Accepted because exposure is dev-only -- the v1 branch is reachable only through the eslint toolchain, has no runtime path, and its inputs are globs written by this team -- and because the alternative (an osv-scanner.toml ignore entry) leaves a suppression someone must remember to remove.
